guidance.escalation-pattern: If {sign}, reach out to your vet clinic

first-night.title: First night at home
first-night.body: Keep the bed close, lights low, and trips outside brief. Quiet whimpering can be normal.
first-night.escalation: Call your clinic if breathing stays fast or the puppy cannot settle at all.

potty-rhythm.title: Potty rhythm
potty-rhythm.body: Offer short outside breaks after sleep, food, and play. Praise calmly the moment it happens outside.
potty-rhythm.escalation: Call your clinic if there is no urination across a full day.

biting-play.title: Mouthing during play
biting-play.body: Pause play when teeth touch skin, then offer a toy before restarting.
biting-play.escalation: Ask a behavior specialist if biting repeatedly breaks adult skin.

crate-settling.title: Crate settling
crate-settling.body: Make the crate a quiet open-door spot first. Add short closed-door moments only when the puppy is calm.
crate-settling.escalation: Pause crate practice and ask for help if panic lasts more than a few minutes.

handling.title: Gentle handling
handling.body: Pair tiny touches on paws, ears, and collar with food so care feels predictable.
handling.escalation: Ask your clinic if touch causes pain, limping, or sudden guarding.

socialization-window.title: Socialization window
socialization-window.body: Choose calm distance, not busy contact. Let the puppy observe people, sounds, and surfaces safely.
socialization-window.escalation: Ask your clinic which outings fit the current vaccine stage.

vet-visit-prep.title: Vet visit prep
vet-visit-prep.body: Practice brief carrier or car moments with treats before the appointment day.
vet-visit-prep.escalation: Call ahead if eating stops, vomiting repeats, or energy drops sharply.

quiet-sleep.title: Quiet sleep
quiet-sleep.body: Protect naps from extra handling. Overtired puppies often bite, bark, or sprint more.
quiet-sleep.escalation: Ask your clinic if sleepiness comes with weakness, fever, or poor appetite.

feeding-rhythm.title: Feeding rhythm
feeding-rhythm.body: Keep meals predictable and log the portion style. Patterns matter more than perfect grams.
feeding-rhythm.escalation: Call your clinic if meals are refused repeatedly or water intake changes suddenly.

alone-time.title: Tiny alone-time steps
alone-time.body: Step away for seconds while the puppy is calm, then return before worry builds.
alone-time.escalation: Ask a trainer if alone time causes panic, drooling, or frantic escape attempts.

leash-intro.title: Leash intro
leash-intro.body: Let the leash appear indoors first, then reward a few relaxed steps beside you.
leash-intro.escalation: Stop and ask for help if the puppy freezes, coughs, or fights the collar.

calm-greetings.title: Calm greetings
calm-greetings.body: Reward four paws on the floor before attention. Keep greetings short and predictable.
calm-greetings.escalation: Ask for training help if jumping turns into repeated nipping.

chew-swap.title: Chew swap
chew-swap.body: Trade household objects for a legal chew instead of chasing or grabbing.
chew-swap.escalation: Call your clinic if anything sharp, toxic, or string-like may have been swallowed.

weekly-rhythm.title: Weekly rhythm
weekly-rhythm.body: At the end of two weeks, compare sleep, potty, and meals to pick one routine to simplify.
weekly-rhythm.escalation: Ask your clinic if a pattern changes abruptly with appetite, stool, or energy.

first-night.title: First night at home
first-night.body: Put the bed near yours. Quiet whimpering is normal. Soft voice, dim lights. In the morning, a short potty break
first-night.escalation: If your puppy is breathing rapidly and can't settle — reach out to your vet clinic

potty-rhythm.title: Potty rhythm
potty-rhythm.body: A small puppy asks to go roughly every 1–2 hours and after eating, sleeping, or playing. Praise calmly the moment they go outside
potty-rhythm.escalation: If there's no urination at all for a full day — call your clinic

biting.title: Mouthing during play
biting.body: Puppies explore the world with their mouth. If teeth touch your hand, say a soft "ow" and pause for 10 seconds. Then offer a toy
biting.escalation: If your puppy repeatedly breaks an adult's skin to the point of pain — talk to a behavior specialist

crate.title: The crate as a quiet spot
crate.body: The crate isn't a punishment — it's a den. Leave treats inside, keep the door open during the day. Sleep in the crate starts with short 10-minute stretches
crate.escalation: If your puppy panics in the crate for more than 15 minutes — stop the training and talk to a specialist
